description:
The first READ reports '22' - a duplicate reported on the base key - and delivers a record with it, and that record is still never displayed. That is the sharpest available statement of what guards the DISPLAY at app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:78: the test at :77 is IF END-OF-FILE = 'N', not 'if a record came back'. The row it delivers is SYNTHESIZED WITH ALL-ZERO NUMERIC FIELDS, and that is the second thing this case pins. THE DERIVATION, exactly: synthesized from app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt row 1 by setting one-based offsets 17-27, CARD-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11), to eleven zeros and one-based offsets 28-30, CARD-CVV-CD PIC 9(03), to three zeros; the other 136 bytes - every character outside those two spans, since 150 - 14 = 136 - are unchanged: CARD-NUM stays 0500024453765740, CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME stays 'Aniya Von' followed by 41 spaces to fill X(50), CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE stays 2023-03-09 carrying the copybook's own misspelling, CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS stays Y, and FILLER stays 59 spaces. The two mutated spans cover fourteen character positions, but the HAMMING DISTANCE FROM THAT ROW IS FOUR, at positions 26, 28, 29 and 30 alone - measured rather than eyeballed (practice B11) - because row 1's account id is already 00000000050 and so already carries nine of the eleven zeros, leaving only its '5' to change. Reading fourteen differing characters off the two span widths is the arithmetic slip this note exists to prevent, and the measured four is what makes the row auditable against the fixture without running anything. THE MUTATION LIVES ONLY IN THIS FILE (practice B3): app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt and its classpath copy at src/test/resources/fixtures/carddata.txt are read-only parity oracle and are NOT edited to add such a row. None of the fifty fixture rows carries an all-zero account id - they run 00000000001 through 00000000050 - and none carries CVV 000, so no fromRow and rowCount range over the fixture can reach this input, which is why the row is declared inline and seeded verbatim. WHY AN ALL-ZERO ROW BELONGS ON THIS ARM SPECIFICALLY: the '22' arm is the one failing arm that reports a record alongside its status, so this row is decoded as a CARD-RECORD before the guard at :77 withholds it - which makes it the one place in this folder where an all-zero numeric span is both delivered and refused. Two verified facts are what that decode pins. FIRST, THERE IS NO SIGN OVERPUNCH TO MODEL ANYWHERE IN A CARD RECORD: app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy declares no COMP-3, no PACKED-DECIMAL and no S9 - verified by search over the whole copybook - so its only two numeric items, CARD-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) and CARD-CVV-CD PIC 9(03), are UNSIGNED zoned DISPLAY and neither carries a sign position. That is what distinguishes carddata from acctdata, tcatbal and dailytran, whose PIC S9(p)V99 money fields close on a zoned overpunch byte in their low-order position; the only overpunch images a card row can legitimately hold are the ones case18 and case19 place inside FILLER, the single span this copybook leaves unconstrained. Adding a sign byte to either numeric span here would be a fabrication, so no overpunch character appears in this row at all. SECOND, A ZONED PIC 9(n) SPAN OCCUPIES ITS FULL DECLARED WIDTH, ZERO-FILLED ON THE LEFT: zero renders as eleven '0' characters at 17-27 and as three at 28-30 - never as a single '0', never as spaces, never as an empty span - so the row still measures exactly 150 characters, which is asserted rather than assumed. A translation holding these as int or long and rendering them naively would emit a shorter or differently-padded field and the total width would break. Zero is also the LOWER BOUNDARY of both unsigned spans, the value on the other side of the guard that refuses a negative into an unsigned picture: case19 carries each of these zeros separately - CVV 000 in its first row and an eleven-zero account id in its second - and this row is the only one in the folder that carries both at once. THE SUPPORTING EVIDENCE IS IN THE FIXTURE ITSELF: row 3 carries CARD-CVV-CD 028, a real leading-zero zoned value that must be carried as the three characters 0, 2 and 8 and never as the integer 28, and every one of the fifty account ids is an eleven-character zero-padded string. All fifty rows' numeric spans are all-digits, verified mechanically. AND CARD-NUM IS NOT A NUMERIC FIELD: the copybook declares it PIC X(16), alphanumeric, so it is deliberately untouched here even though its sixteen characters happen to be digits. Conflating a digit-bearing X span with a 9 span is the easy mistake on this record, and both mutations above are confined to the two spans that really are PIC 9. THE RUN, once into app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:70-87 and no further. :71 displays the 38-character start banner. :72 performs 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN, whose OPEN INPUT at :120 reports '00', so :121 takes its first arm and :126-127 CONTINUE. The PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' at :74-81 begins its first iteration, :75 finds END-OF-FILE = 'N' and :76 performs 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT. The READ at :93 reports '22': :94's CARDFILE-STATUS = '00' is false and so is :98's = '10', so :101 MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT runs; :104 finds the 88-level APPL-AOK false and :107 finds APPL-EOF false, so the error arm at :110-113 runs in order - :110 displays the 22-character 'ERROR READING CARDFILE', :111 moves the status into IO-STATUS, :112 performs 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and :113 performs 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM, whose :155 displays the 16-character 'ABENDING PROGRAM' before :158 CALL 'CEE3ABD'. Control never returns to the mainline, so :78 never displays the record the read delivered, :83's 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE never runs, and :85's end banner is never written. RETURN-CODE is the 12 that :101 moved into APPL-RESULT, carried out by the abend rather than by GOBACK (gate G35), and a batch exit status carries that value to the process - which is what makes a JCL COND test on a following step behave as it does today. THE STATUS IMAGE IS DERIVED, not guessed: IO-STATUS holds '22', which is numeric, and IO-STAT1 is not '9', so 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS takes its ELSE - :170 moves '0000' into IO-STATUS-04 and :171 moves IO-STATUS into IO-STATUS-04(3:2), leaving 0022 - and :172 displays the literal 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by it, giving the 24-character line below. That literal genuinely ends in four N characters; they are source text, not a placeholder for the digits that follow. In repository terms the sequence is startBrowse '00', then readNext '22', then the abend: there is no readNext '10' and no endBrowse on this path, and that truncation is itself the assertion (gate G47). The job is driven at tasklet and step level, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP anywhere in the path (gate G51). MESSAGE ARITHMETIC: 1 start banner + 1 read-error line + 1 status line + 1 abend line = 4 ordered DISPLAY_LINE entries, of 38, 22, 24 and 16 characters. NO 150-CHARACTER IMAGE APPEARS AMONG THEM, and that absence is the case: the row is seeded, delivered, decoded and withheld, so a translation that displayed whatever the read handed back, or that treated a delivered record as success, would emit a line here that the COBOL does not - and one that read an all-zero account id and CVV as an empty or absent record would take a different branch entirely. :96's DISPLAY is a COMMENT and no display paragraph exists, so :78 is the only live display of a record and it is never reached. RECORD GEOMETRY, taken mechanically from app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy (01 CARD-RECORD, RECLN 150) rather than counted off a line by eye, one-based with cumulative ends: CARD-NUM PIC X(16) at 1-16, cumulative 16, and also the RECORD KEY at :32; CARD-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) at 17-27, cumulative 27; CARD-CVV-CD PIC 9(03) at 28-30, cumulative 30; CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME PIC X(50) at 31-80, cumulative 80; CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE PIC X(10) at 81-90, cumulative 90; CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS PIC X(01) at 91, cumulative 91; FILLER PIC X(59) at 92-150, cumulative 150. 16+11+3+50+10+1+59 = 150 (gate G19), and the seeded row ends in FILLER's 59 significant spaces, which must not be trimmed (gate G21). THE MISSPELLING IS THE CONTRACT: the copybook spells the date field CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE, missing the second T, exactly as CVACT01Y spells its own ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE. It is preserved verbatim and never corrected, because field-for-field diffing keys on the name (AAP implicit requirement I1). WHAT THIS CASE PINS ABOUT THE UNIT: it is account.AccountBalanceReaderJob - an Account-named class in the account package - yet CBACT02C computes no balance and never opens the account file. It reads the CARD file. :29-33 is SELECT CARDFILE-FILE ASSIGN TO CARDFILE, ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL, RECORD KEY IS FD-CARD-NUM, FILE STATUS IS CARDFILE-STATUS; :37-40 is an FD of FD-CARD-NUM X(16) plus FD-CARD-DATA X(134) = 150; and :45 is COPY CVACT02Y. AAP rule R1 governs - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and the divergence is catalogued in the register at AAP 0.8.4. A reviewer who trusts the class name will look for the wrong file and the wrong arithmetic. REACHABILITY, stated plainly: '22' cannot be produced by browsing this base cluster over the seeded row, so the status is induced by the run shape declared for this case rather than by the data - which is exactly what a case is for when seeded data cannot reach a real arm. The arm itself is real: :101 catches every status other than '00' and '10', and case16 is the open-side counterpart that reports the same '22' from :121 instead. This is also the case the return-code perturbation guard borrows, because proving the comparison has teeth needs a run that genuinely abends; a case completing with zero, perturbed to zero, would compare against itself and report clean while claiming the opposite. WIRING: app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:22 is a bare //STEP05 EXEC PGM=CBACT02C, the job declares no PARM anywhere and CBACT02C has no LINKAGE SECTION to receive one into, so jobParameters is empty; its single //CARDFILE DD at :25-26 is the only dataset seeded, addressed solely by the CARDFILE binding key that application.yml resolves at record length 150, so no dataset-name literal appears anywhere in this file (gate G46). ENCODING is US-ASCII, named explicitly rather than left to a platform default. NOTHING IS WRITTEN: expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty, and that emptiness is a positive assertion rather than an absence of interest - :120 opens the file INPUT and the program contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE at all, its only output being SYSOUT at app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:27 - and no normalisation is declared, because this row is already the full 150 bytes CVACT02Y declares, so neither recorded fixture-to-copybook deviation applies here. PROVENANCE: every expected value in this file is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl, cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy for every offset and width, app/jcl/READCARD.jcl for the step and DD contract, and the real app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt for the 136 bytes outside the two rewritten spans, which this row inherits verbatim. It was NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution: AAP 0.7.6 proves such a run impossible in this environment with eight independently verified blockers - no z/OS runtime, the available compiler's indexed file handler disabled, subprogram linkage that cannot be made executable, a copybook that will not parse, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator alongside three absent IBM copybooks, EBCDIC fixtures needing binary handling, and no alternative compiler installable - and the substitution of provenance is recorded as risk R-A (practice B12). Only the provenance changes; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diff and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand. GATES PINNED HERE: G15 (one of the twenty cases for this program), G18 (its diff count must be zero), G19 and G21 (the 150-byte width and the significant FILLER spaces), G35 (the CEE3ABD site raising an abend that carries RETURN-CODE 12), G46 (binding key, never a DSNAME), G47 (the status sequence, truncated at the failing read) and G51 (asserted below the HTTP and JobLauncher layers). NOT APPLICABLE: G30 and G32, since CBACT02C contains no GO TO; G33, since it declares no OCCURS; G16 and both right-pad normalisations, since carddata.txt needs neither; G20, since this program writes no record; G22 through G28, since CVACT02Y declares no V99 span at all and this program performs no arithmetic beyond its own status bookkeeping, so the BigDecimal and RoundingMode.DOWN gates have no subject here; and G37 through G43, since no screen is driven. One all-zero-numeric row seeded, one delivered, none displayed, four lines out, RETURN-CODE 12.

HOW THE OUTCOME IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges a first READ that reports DFHRESP(DUPREC), which carries a record the loop still refuses to display: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names READ-CARDFILE and gives it RESP 14 after 0 record(s) have been delivered. It is declared here because a case identifier must name a case and never configure one - the shape used to be chosen by a switch over 'case01'..'case20' in CBACT02CParityTest, so this file showed the abend lines and said nothing about the condition that produced them, and renumbering a case silently changed what it ran. A case that names no call site reads its whole input and closes cleanly, so silence here is itself a statement. The outcome is a CICS RESP rather than a FILE STATUS because CardRepository reports this program's card-file outcomes as responses and AccountBalanceReaderJob translates them - declaring a status directly would skip the translation the case exists to judge.
